digo_source: Pakia (2005) App. III (Mtandarusi); Maundu & Tengnäs 2005 (Msandarusi, Munyama)
english: Gum copal tree, East African copal

teaser.en: Its gum once lights homes at night and keeps pests out of the maize store.

summary.en: *Mtandarusi*, the gum copal tree, is an evergreen tree of the coastal forests of Kwale and Kilifi with beautifully patterned bark. It produces gum copal, *sandarusi*, prized for varnish and glue and burned for light and to protect stored maize.

about.en: *Mtandarusi* is an evergreen tree from 6 to 25 metres tall. Its bark is smooth and pale grey, patterned with patches of green, pink and cream. Each leaf is just one pair of glossy leaflets, asymmetric in shape. The pods are warty.

where.en: It grows in coastal forest, woodland and evergreen bushland in Kwale and Kilifi.

uses.en:
The tree's great product is gum copal, *sandarusi*, collected from the bark and from fallen fruit. It is prized for varnish and glue. The gum is burned to light homes at night, and its smoke keeps storage pests out of maize granaries.

The tree also gives hard timber and canoes, and its fruit is edible.

culture.en: Pakia records that its seeds are called *tembe za mtandarusi*.

names.en: Pakia records the Digo name *mtandarusi*; the ICRAF handbook gives *msandarusi* and *munyama*. In Swahili it is *mtandarusi* or *msandarusi*, and the gum is *sandarusi*. Giriama names are *mdzongolo* and *msange*. In English it is the gum copal tree or East African copal.

reason.en: Its seeds are also called tembe

definition.en: The seeds of the copal tree. They have no use, so they are called 'seeds of …'; the useful timber goes by the tree's own name.

sources: Pakia, M. (2005) African Traditional Plant Knowledge Today: an ethnobotanical study of the Digo at the Kenya Coast. PhD thesis, Univ. Bayreuth, Appendix III (Digo–botanical name list) & Appendix VI (name semantics). https://epub.uni-bayreuth.de/881/1/Pakia.pdf
Maundu, P. & Tengnäs, B. (eds) (2005) Useful Trees and Shrubs for Kenya, ICRAF — sheet Hymenaea verrucosa: https://apps.worldagroforestry.org/usefultrees/pdflib/Hymenaea_verrucosa_KEN.pdf
Ngumbau, V.M. et al. (2020) An annotated checklist of the coastal forests of Kenya. PhytoKeys 147:1–191. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7237506/
